## Sandbox

The "Sandbox" section is headed "Sandbox", with a muted line beneath saying, in one sentence, that each run can reach only what its mode allows, enforced by the operating system, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says. It is laid out as a column of cards, each a box on the theme's raised surface with corners rounded 6 pixels and 12 pixels of padding, 16 pixels apart, each headed by its name in small semibold text, so every part reads as a block of its own. From top to bottom come Status, always shown; Who can see what, Code and spec, and Spec tasks, for the open project; and Outside the sandbox, always shown. With no project open, only Status and Outside the sandbox show, with a muted line between them saying the rest is for a project, once one is open.

## Sandbox Status

The Status card is one line: a dot, green while the sandbox can enforce every profile here and red while it can't, then the backend's name, "Landlock", "Seatbelt", or "AppContainer", and, muted, what it enforces on this machine in plain words, as "files and local sockets". At its right, a small ghost "Test" button runs the short set of hostile checks the sandbox is tested with, in a temporary project, showing a spinner meanwhile, and then a summary beneath the line, "12 of 12 refused" in green, or "1 of 12 got through" in the theme's error colour, which expands to list each check with a tick or a cross. Where the sandbox can't run, the line is in the theme's error colour and says why in plain words, as "This kernel has no Landlock", that no task or question will run until it can, and links to the sandbox's documentation; Test is then disabled.

## Sandbox Profiles

The Who can see what card is a small grid, so each run's reach is seen at a glance: the project's areas down its left, Code, Spec source, Compiled reference, Project data, and Everything else, and the modes across its top, Code, Spec, Ask, and Freeform, each in its mode's colour. Each cell is a small label: "Edit", on a faint tint of the theme's success colour; "Read", on a faint tint of its accent; or "No access", muted and untinted. Hovering a cell shows the paths it covers. Beneath the grid, one muted line says what every mode can reach outside the project, as "System and toolchains read only; the harness's folders, build caches, and a temporary folder editable". The grid follows the classification and the Spec tasks switches as they change, so a change shows at once what it allows.

## Sandbox Classification

The Code and spec card says, muted, which parts of the project are code and which are spec, and that a Code run can't open spec and a Spec run can't open code. It holds two lists side by side, "Code", headed in Code's colour, and "Spec", in Spec's, each a column of rows, one per folder or pattern, in monospace, with a small remove button at its right shown on hover. Beneath each list, "Add folder" opens the folder browser in the project, and "Add pattern" adds a row to type a pattern into, as `**/*.pi`, saved once Enter is pressed or it loses focus. A row in both lists is marked in the theme's error colour in each, with a line beneath the card saying runs won't start until it is in one only. At the card's foot, a small ghost "Reset to project locations" button is enabled only while the lists differ from the project's code and spec locations. Each change is saved to `.suspense/sandbox.json` straight away, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says.

## Sandbox Spec Tasks

The Spec tasks card holds two switches, each a row with its label at the left, a muted line under it saying what it does, and the switch at the right: "Read the code", saying Spec tasks can read the code but never change it, and, indented beneath it and shown only while it is on, "Read the whole project", saying they can also read the rest of the project, read only. Both start off, are saved with the project, and take effect from the next run.

## Sandbox Outside

The Outside the sandbox card lists, muted, in three short lines each with a small icon, what the sandbox doesn't cover, so it is never mistaken for protection: the network, the harness's own service, and the clipboard, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox)'s channels say, each with one plain sentence saying why it matters.

## Saving

content.text:
I rebuilt the Sandbox settings page as the spec describes, and it type-checks and passes its tests. I haven't seen it rendered, and I couldn't build it in the project folder itself (explained below).

- **Status:** one line with a green or red dot, the backend's name and what it enforces in plain words ("files and local sockets"). A ghost "Test" button runs 12 hostile checks and shows "12 of 12 refused" (or "N of 12 got through" in red), which expands to each check with a tick or cross. When the sandbox can't run, the line goes red, says why, and Test is disabled.
- **Who can see what:** a grid with Code, Spec source, Compiled reference, Project data and Everything else down the side, and Code, Spec, Ask and Freeform across the top in their colours. Each cell reads Edit, Read or No access, and hovering shows the paths it covers. It is worked out from the profiles as they compile, so it changes as soon as you edit the lists or flip a switch.
- **Code and spec:** two side-by-side lists with "Add folder" and "Add pattern" (saved on Enter or when the field loses focus). Each row has a remove button shown on hover. Anything in both lists turns red, with a line saying runs won't start. "Reset to project locations" is only enabled when the lists differ from the project's locations.
- **Spec tasks:** two switches, each with a one-line explanation; the second appears only while the first is on.
- **Outside the sandbox:** the network, the harness's service and the clipboard, each with an icon and a sentence on why it matters.
- **No project open:** only Status and Outside the sandbox show, with a muted line between them.

**Why I couldn't build here:** this session ran under Suspense's own Code sandbox, which blocked two things the build needs:
- It refuses reading `.suspense/system-prompts/`, which the build embeds.
- Its `piton` shim refuses the `piton compile` that `build.rs` runs on the baked prompts.

So I type-checked and tested a copy of the code with those prompt files stubbed and the real `piton` on the path. There, the build has no errors or warnings, and the 24 sandbox, settings and welcome tests pass, including a new one for this page.

**Two things for you to decide:**
- **Code roots for this repo:** add `.suspense/system-prompts` as a code root in Settings → Sandbox, so Code runs can build Suspense.
- **Allowing `piton compile`:** the spec says Code runs may only `piton slice --adapter`, but this repository's own build needs `piton compile` for its baked prompts. Allowing that would be a change to the spec.

**Fix found along the way:** tests run from inside a sandboxed run picked up its `GIT_DIR`, so the filtered-repository code found the wrong repository. Its `git` lookups now ignore an inherited `GIT_DIR`, and the tests' own setup commands clear it.
